base_data_requirements.fallback: volume-weighted average inbound unit_price across the material's supply lanes; the cheapest quoted price when no lane carries a volume
base_data_requirements.reason: Inventory valuation and holding cost — the terminal default of 1.0 makes every cost KPI meaningless.
Revenue and lost-sales valuation — the terminal default of 1.0 makes revenue KPIs meaningless.
Demand generation — with neither source the product is never ordered (zero demand).
With no capacity source the engine defaults to max(2·demand, 1000), so plant capacity never binds.
Purchase cost per sourcing arc — a missing price defaults to 1.0 and distorts procurement spend.
Supplier lead time per sourcing arc — missing values default to 2 weeks.

empty_means.meaning: No capacity limit. An empty supplier capacity means unlimited, so this supplier never throttles shipments — and a partial-magnitude disruption on it degrades to a full outage. Enter a number to model a finite capacity.

base_data_requirements.reason: Empty means unlimited (a valid modeling choice) — but partial-magnitude supplier disruptions need a finite capacity to throttle, else they degrade to full outages.

bom_line.description: r_{p,m} — §3.2. ALL listed materials are required (hard constraint, Eq. 8).
bom_line.title: BomLine

customer.description: Customer segments — §3.1. Needed by P-C.2; inert for single-customer MTO.
customer.title: Customer

lane.title: Lane

initial_on_hand.notes: None → initialized to the order-up-to level S_m at t=0 (warm start).
initial_on_hand.title: Initial On Hand

demand_floor_factor.title: Demand Floor Factor

fg_base_stock.notes: S^FG_p; derived if None. MTS only.
fg_base_stock.title: Fg Base Stock

bootstrap_resamples.notes: Percentile bootstrap on Δ and synergy metrics.
bootstrap_resamples.title: Bootstrap Resamples

crn_enabled.notes: Common random numbers; required for synergy math.
crn_enabled.title: Crn Enabled

detection_lag_weeks.notes: Delay between physical disruption start and firm knowledge (PH-20). Manuscript core uses 0; P-S.4 early_warning_failover governs this lever.
detection_lag_weeks.title: Detection Lag Weeks

disruption_event_seeds.notes: (start, duration, magnitude) draws. Collapses to 1 when all events are fixed.

project_seed.title: Project Seed

replication_stopping.notes: sequential_ci stops when FR CI half-width ≤ ε.

trace_verbosity.notes: Stress tests default to kpi_only (≈100× less IO).

warmup_end.notes: t_w. Required when warmup_method=manual; auto-detected otherwise. Manuscript: 85.
warmup_end.title: Warmup End

warmup_method.notes: Runs Conway and MSER-5, adopts the later week.

simulation_settings.title: SimulationSettings

capacity_per_week.notes: None = ∞ (manuscript). Finite required for capacity_reduction events and P-S.3.
capacity_per_week.title: Capacity Per Week

tier.notes: Reserved extension point; v1 simulates tier 1 only.
tier.title: Tier

lead_time_dist.notes: Stochastic lead times consume the world leadtime stream only when an order is placed; CRN caveat documented in docs/statistics.md.

kpis.definition: Value-weighted served demand: Σ u_p·served_p / Σ u_p·D_p over the analysis window (Eq. 10); weekly FR[t] recorded in the trace.
kpis.name: fill_rate

kpis.definition: Σ u_p · L_p over the window.
kpis.name: lost_sales_value

kpis.definition: mat-SS holding + backup premiums + multi-sourcing premiums + expediting + overtime + lost sales + allocation labor + FG-SS holding (MTS) + backorder penalties (Eq. 23).
kpis.name: cost_of_resilience

kpis.definition: 1 − C^res_i / C^res_S0, CRN-paired per replication (Eq. 24-style); positive = cheaper than do-nothing.
kpis.name: delta_cost

kpis.definition: Σu_p(Q_i − Q_S0) / Σu_p(D − Q_S0), CRN-paired (Eq. 25-style); share of S0's lost revenue recovered.
kpis.name: delta_revenue

kpis.definition: Weeks from disruption start until weekly FR re-enters the pre-disruption band (3-week sustained); 0 if FR never left the band.
kpis.name: ttr_weeks

kpis.definition: Weeks from disruption start that FR survives inside the band (time-to-survive under the shock).
kpis.name: tts_weeks

kpis.definition: ∫ max(0, FR_clean − FR_disrupted) dt over the window, CRN-paired against the same portfolio without events.
kpis.name: service_loss_area

kpis.definition: Peak Σ_p B_p within the window.
kpis.name: max_backlog

kpis.definition: Δ_portfolio − Σ Δ_components, CRN-paired, percentile-bootstrap stars.
kpis.name: synergy_R / synergy_C

kpis.definition: 100·[w1(1−ŠLA) + w2(1−ŤTR) + w3·ŤTS + w4(1−Č)], w=(.35,.25,.15,.25) editable; components always shown.
kpis.name: resilience_index

phases.description: Onset/recovery profiles → physical disruption state for the week.
phases.name: week_start

phases.name: demand_realization

phases.name: detection

phases.description: MTS serves D_p from I^FG; no-op for MTO products.
phases.name: fulfill_from_stock

phases.name: production_planning

phases.name: production_execute

phases.name: material_planning

phases.description: Order release (Eqs. 4–6) and sourcing decisions; orders enter the supplier queue.
phases.name: procurement

phases.description: Ship queue under capacity gating, defer in-window arrivals (Eqs. 11–12), expedite (Eqs. 18–19), land arrivals.
phases.name: logistics

phases.description: Read-only KPI rows, cost rollup, trace.
phases.name: accounting

partial_accept_prob.notes: Share of unmet demand that waits.
partial_accept_prob.title: Partial Accept Prob

policies.summary: What happens to an unservable order: it dies (lost_sales — competitive markets), waits (backorder — contractual B2B), or splits (partial_backorder). Backorders convert lost revenue into delay cost, changing the economics of every strategy.

data_requirements.reason: Per-customer demand shares come from outbound volumes; without them there are no customer segments to allocate between (the policy is inert below two customers).

data_requirements.fallback: Customer.priority_weight's own default, 1.0 — every customer equal, which makes the `priority` rule inert
data_requirements.reason: The `priority` rule orders customers by this weight wherever the `priority_weights` param does not name the customer (SimContext.cust_priority). Only the RATIO between two customers means anything, so a table where every row is unset cannot order anything.

data_requirements.fallback: Customer.segment's own default, "default" — every customer in one segment, so no `sla_tiers` key can match and every declared floor resolves to 0.0
data_requirements.reason: `sla_tiers` maps segment → fill floor %, so the segment is the axis the `sla_tier` rule tiers on (SimContext.cust_segment). It is also what the `fill_rate_segment_<segment>` KPIs are keyed by.

rule.notes: fcfs/proportional/fair_share coincide at weekly buckets (pro-rata); priority and sla_tier reorder.
rule.title: Rule

sla_tiers.notes: Guaranteed first-pass fill per segment; scaled down pro-rata when supply cannot honor all floors.
sla_tiers.title: Sla Tiers

policies.summary: Under scarcity, 'who do we disappoint first' is deliberate — protect strategic accounts / SLA tiers / spread pain. Inert for single-customer MTO. Hook: PH-60.
Move demand instead of fighting supply — substitution offers, delay incentives; cheap when customers accept. Hook: PH-60.

visibility_horizon.notes: τ* — how far ahead the committed order book is visible to the plant. None → settings.visibility_horizon (the schedule length); must not exceed it.
visibility_horizon.title: Visibility Horizon

policies.summary: Customer commits future orders over a visibility horizon τ* (§III-D.6), so the plant can size coverage against the forward order book instead of a stationary mean — the customer-side half of the Forward-visible basis (§II.4). Hook: PH-10.

data_requirements.reason: Minimum order quantity rounds up PH-80 order releases.
Holding cost rate prices the inventory this policy carries.

ModeStrip.description:
nominal/alert/crisis parameter strip (Part IV header). v1 engines use
nominal normally and crisis while any event is firm-visible; alert engages
once P-S.4 early warning lands (M7).
ModeStrip.title: ModeStrip

basis.notes: Policy Basis (§II.4): days_of_supply sizes levels from the stationary mean (s = E[D_m]·T_s); forward_visible sums the committed forward order book over the coverage window (WSC-2026 MTO) — requires the P-C.6 forward_visibility customer policy.
basis.title: Basis

coverage_weeks.notes: κ — order-up-to cover beyond lead time. Strip 8/10/12.

policies.summary: Everyday replenishment rule (min-max / base-stock / (R,Q) / periodic). The baseline shock absorber every chain already has; quantifying it prevents over-buying dedicated resilience.
Convert lines to new capability mid-crisis (Intel substrate) — high cost, delay, true bounce-forward. Hook: PH-40.
Batching exists for setup economics but can amplify shocks (bullwhip) — test whether your lots worsen propagation. Hook: PH-80.

data_requirements.reason: Safety-stock sizing scales with demand variability; the default CV of 0.30 may badly misstate your buffers.

hooks.resolution: Adds the safety-stock buffer on top of inventory_control's levels (priority 50) — Eqs. 20–21.

abc_breakpoints.notes: A up to 80%, B up to 95%, C the rest (80/15/5).
abc_breakpoints.title: Abc Breakpoints

policies.summary: ABC-XYZ-differentiated material safety stock (Eqs. 20–21). Dominates short disruptions; depletes — beyond ~7–9 weeks expediting wins (run the crossover sweep).

data_requirements.reason: Revenue-based ABC segmentation ranks products by price x demand; the 1.0 price default collapses the classes.
FG buffer sizing scales with demand variability.

hooks.resolution: Adds the FG safety stock on top of the cycle-stock base target written by mech.fg_target_base (priority 45) — ADR 0001.

segmentation.notes: abc_by_revenue: A = configured SL, B −2 pp, C −5 pp (floor 80).
segmentation.title: Segmentation

policies.summary: The only buffer DOWNSTREAM of production (MTS only): keeps serving customers while production is blocked, and is the only feasible buffer when suppliers are single-sourced. Costs full COGS per unit held — versus P-P.3, likely submodular for short disruptions (same window, opposite sides of the CODP).

data_requirements.fallback: production policy capacity_units_per_day x 7 x utilization
data_requirements.reason: Overtime only bites when base capacity binds; the engine default max(2*demand, 1000) never binds, making this policy a silent no-op.

policies.summary: Overtime: pay-per-use plant headroom (Eq. 22). Bites only when production capacity binds — in material-constrained networks that is rare; check utilization first.
Permanently maintained plant headroom — option premium vs P-P.5's pay-per-use. Hook: PH-40.
Which lines make which products; Jordan–Graves chaining — a little flexibility buys most of the value. Hook: PH-40.
Pre-qualified substitutes (Tesla chip-redesign pattern) — the only material-side answer to single-sourced bottlenecks; qualification must precede the crisis. Hooks: PH-40/PH-50.

data_requirements.reason: Revenue-weighted allocation objectives need real product prices to rank products.

hooks.resolution: Replaces the default greedy plan (priority 50 mechanic) with the rolling-LP allocation when active.

policies.summary: The weekly war-room as a rolling LP (Eqs. 13–17): reassign shared materials across products to protect revenue during scarcity. Costs planner time only; value scales with the shared-material index.

data_requirements.reason: The min_cost reroute selection rule compares supplier prices; missing prices default to 1.0.
The reliability selection rule ranks backup sources by this score.

hooks.resolution: Reroutes orders released by inventory_control (priority 50) away from firm-visibly disrupted primary suppliers.

backup_lead_time_weeks.notes: T_{s′} override; None → the backup link's own lead time. Plan default 6.
backup_lead_time_weeks.title: Backup Lead Time Weeks

cooldown_weeks.notes: Keep using the backup this long after the event clears.
cooldown_weeks.title: Cooldown Weeks

coverage_threshold_weeks.notes: Reroute only when position covers fewer weeks than this.
coverage_threshold_weeks.title: Coverage Threshold Weeks

enabled_materials.notes: Materials covered; single-sourced ones are skipped.
enabled_materials.title: Enabled Materials

policies.summary: Contingent rerouting to a qualified backup source — premium paid only on rerouted orders. Slower than warm dual-sourcing, and useless when a BoM peer is single-sourced: one missing material still blocks the product.

data_requirements.reason: Standing order splits derive source weights from lane volumes when explicit ratios are not set.

hooks.resolution: Splits the orders released by inventory_control (priority 50) across qualified links; P-S.1 (priority 60) may still reroute a disrupted slice afterwards.

min_share_pct.notes: Smallest viable slice; caps how many sources the default split spreads across.
min_share_pct.title: Min Share Pct

rebalance_trigger.notes: disruption: shift shares away from firm-visibly disrupted suppliers. reliability_drop lands with reliability dynamics (M8).
rebalance_trigger.title: Rebalance Trigger

secondary_premium.notes: Contractual premium on non-primary slices, on top of the link cost difference.
secondary_premium.title: Secondary Premium

weights.notes: w_{m,s}; each material's shares sum to 100. Materials absent here use the default equal split.
weights.title: Weights

policies.summary: Split orders across warm sources in NORMAL operations — no activation delay, permanent premium; the structural answer to capacity-cut events. Pay-always vs P-S.1's pay-on-activation; each slice carries its own source's lead time, so a disruption hits only its slice.
Real-options contract (semiconductor-style): standing fee for callable capacity; reserved units bypass capacity cuts. Cheaper than stock for slow, expensive materials. Hook: PH-80.

hooks.resolution: Compresses the detection lag the mechanic (priority 50) applies when serving firm knowledge: effective lag = min(monitored, scenario). Later residents see the compressed view.

detection_lag_weeks.notes: Monitored disruption-start → firm-knows delay; the effective lag is min(this, settings.detection_lag_weeks). Applies to ALL reactive strategies (PH-20).
detection_lag_weeks.title: Detection Lag Weeks

monitoring_cost.notes: Standing visibility cost, charged weekly (÷52) into C^res whether or not a disruption occurs.
monitoring_cost.title: Monitoring Cost

policies.summary: Visibility investments compress disruption-start → firm-knows. Makes 'what is a week of warning worth?' a first-class experiment. Hook: PH-20.
Qualified alternative lanes/modes per supplier — edge-risk redundancy; prerequisite for P-T.3 mode_shift. Hook: PH-90.

hooks.resolution: Runs after the deferral mechanic (priority 10) and before landing (priority 90): expedited quantities land this week at a premium.

policies.summary: Premium freight pulls existing in-transit forward (Eqs. 18–19) — repeatable every week, hence the strongest long-disruption strategy. Cannot conjure units a capacity cut never shipped (supplier queue is out of reach).
Switch NEW orders to a faster lane (sea→air) — composable with P-T.2, which moves the EXISTING flow. Hooks: PH-80/PH-90.
Order earlier than policy dictates for long-lead/critical materials — a time buffer instead of a unit buffer. Hook: PH-70.

Firms execute SEQUENCED responses — detect → expedite → backup → overtime — gated by triggers and budget. Composes enabled policies; replaces flat recovery lists. Hook: PH-20 (evaluation) + delegated.

policy_bundle_keys.transform: fraction x 100 into the material's weight map, keyed by supplier; only for a supplier the material actually has a link to
enum map — min_max/s_S/continuous_review -> min_max, base_stock -> base_stock, rop -> rop_q, periodic_review -> periodic; anything unrecognised falls back to min_max
days, clamped 0-84. Only when `safety_stock_method` is neither service_level/demand_variability nor king_method — those two take a different classification and this key is not read
fraction x 100, clamped 80.0-99.9. Read only when `safety_stock_method` is service_level or demand_variability
units/day x 7 x utilization_cap_pct (default 0.85) -> units/week. The MASTER `products.production_capacity` shadows it entirely when present, and the mapper warns that the grid entry is not applied

percent / 100, multiplied into the weekly capacity above; the mapper substitutes 85 when the production policy sets none and says so. Read ONLY on the branch that derives capacity from the grid — a master production_capacity shadows this too
enum — 'none' skips the policy; 'service_level' selects service-level sizing; anything else selects fixed_days. Gated on the engine's own `has_mts`, not on the policy's fulfillment_strategy string
fraction x 100, clamped 80.0-99.9. Read only when `fg_safety_stock` is service_level
days, clamped 0-12. Read only when `fg_safety_stock` selects fixed_days sizing

per-product weight, collected from composite `node:<node>::<product>` override keys. Read only when the scenario asks for `allocate_materials`, and its presence switches the objective to priority_weighted

stress_tests.description: Supplier outage sweep (manuscript): each supplier × LT-extension × Δt {5,8,10}.
Supplier capacity-cut sweep: each supplier × φ {0.75,0.5,0.25,0} × {4,8} wks.
Nexus-node attack: top-k ML-critical (M7; ml-service integration).
